intro.title: Build typed notification payloads
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple notification system using TypeScript. You will create typed objects to represent different notification payloads, such as success, error, and warning messages. The core concept is using TypeScript's type annotations to define the shape and allowed properties of these payloads. You will work with interfaces and type aliases to ensure your data is structured correctly. By the end, you'll have a set of reusable, type-safe notification objects ready for use in an application.
intro.usecase: Typed notification payloads are essential in modern applications where different notification types require structured data. In e-commerce dashboards, order confirmations need product details and tracking numbers, while security alerts require timestamps and severity levels. Messaging apps use typed payloads to distinguish between text messages, file uploads, and system notifications, each with different required fields. This pattern ensures notifications are validated at compile time, preventing runtime errors when displaying critical information to users.
